learning_objective: 🎯 Step into the business of fashion! Learn how trends are born, how the fashion cycle works, and how clothes get from a designer's sketchbook to your closet.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Style is a specific characteristic of a look. Fashion is a style accepted by the majority at a given time. A Fad is a short-lived trend, while a Classic never goes out of style (like a white button-down shirt).
Fashion follows a bell curve: Introduction (designers show new styles), Rise (influencers adopt it), Peak (mass popularity), Decline (people get bored), and Obsolescence (style is rejected).
Haute Couture refers to exclusive, custom-fitted, high-end fashion made by hand. Prêt-à-Porter (Ready-to-Wear) is mass-produced in standardized sizes for the general public.
Merchandising is the business side of fashion. It ensures that the right merchandise is available at the right time, in the right place, in the right quantities, and at the right price.
Fashion Designers create the concepts, Fashion Merchandisers plan the buying and selling, and Retailers sell the final products to consumers.

fun_activity.title: 🔥 Fad vs. Classic Hunt
fun_activity.instructions: Open a fashion app or look at an old photo album. Identify 3 'Fads' (things that were super popular for just a few months, like neon chunky sneakers) and 3 'Classics' (things people have worn for decades, like blue jeans).

exam_tips: 📌 You must be able to draw and label the 5 stages of the Fashion Cycle.
📌 Distinguish between Style, Fashion, Fad, and Classic with specific examples.
📌 Memorize the 'Five Rights' of Merchandising: Right Merchandise, Right Place, Right Time, Right Quantity, Right Price.
quick_recap: ⭐ The fashion industry is driven by consumer acceptance; if people don't buy it, it's not fashion.
⭐ Fast fashion has drastically shortened the fashion cycle, causing trends to peak and decline rapidly.
⭐ Merchandising bridges the gap between the creative design process and the final retail consumer.
